state:
Goal `core-str-2-3`, 2 of 3 items done. `Core\Str::graphemes` and `Core\Str::indexOf` are complete
(`bun nv proofs --id` says so for each): description, three examples, attack, bench with a perf record,
Rust test and a plain card each. The `indexOf` attack found a linear-time bug in the case-insensitive
search. It is fixed in `find_from` (Knuth–Morris–Pratt over each character's lower-case mapping) and
pinned by `tests/conformance/core/str-index-of-case-insensitive-near-miss-is-linear.nvst`. A second
finding, a match that starts or ends inside one grapheme, is recorded as gap
`nvs-stdlib/a-match-inside-a-character-reports-the-wrong-position` (owner M11), because the fix is a
choice between two semantics for the whole search family. `str.rs` now has a `# Known gaps` heading.

next.title: feature proofs, one member per slice

items.text: **`Core\Str::isEmpty`** — owes examples, hostile, perf, tests, and its `about.md` and a plain card (`rule:testing/feature-proofs`). `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs:210`

backlog: `Core\Str::lastIndexOf` walks every overlapping match with a fresh `find_at`, so `"a"` × N with an `"a"` × M needle costs N·M in both modes; the attack for it will find this — `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs` `nvs_core_str_last_index_of`.

`Core\Str::replaceAll` tries every needle at every position, so one long needle that almost matches costs text length × needle length in both modes — `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/str.rs` `nvs_core_str_replace_all`.
A match inside one grapheme: gap `nvs-stdlib/a-match-inside-a-character-reports-the-wrong-position`, owner M11.
